root_cause: The date picker's keydown handler (_onKeyChange) does not explicitly handle the Tab key (keyCode 9), and the picker's focusable internal elements (day buttons, previous/next month buttons) lack tabindex="-1", causing them to remain in the tab order. Additionally, the picker container itself may be inadvertently focusable. When the picker is open, pressing Tab from the date input moves focus into the picker instead of to the next form field (#guests).
repair_strategy: 1. Add an explicit no-op case for keyCode 9 in _onKeyChange to ensure the handler does not interfere with Tab. 2. Add tabindex="-1" to all focusable buttons within the picker (day buttons, previous/next month buttons) to remove them from the sequential tab order. 3. Add tabindex="-1" to the picker container (the .pika-single element) to ensure it is not in the tab order. 4. Verify that month/year selects already have tabindex="-1" (they do in the original source).

expected_accessibility_effect: After entering a date in the check-in field and pressing Tab, focus will move to the guests field, enabling keyboard-only users to continue filling the form without interruption. Arrow keys will still navigate the picker when it is open.
functional_risks: Adding tabindex="-1" to the picker container makes it programmatically focusable but not in the tab order; no known functionality relies on tabbing to the container.
Adding a no-op case for Tab could theoretically interfere with any future custom handling of Tab, but no such handling exists in the current code.
verification_requirements: Confirm that typing a date and pressing Tab moves focus to the guests field.
Verify that arrow keys (left/right/up/down) still adjust the date when the picker is open.
Ensure that Enter and Escape still close the picker and blur the field as expected.
Check that manual date entry via keyboard continues to update the field correctly.
Verify that mouse interaction with picker buttons still works.
